    ip = "20.0.0.1"          # public, not in EXCLUDE_RANGES
    # return up to 8 identical argument lists; the harness can repeat the list n times
    return [[ip] for _ in range(min(n, 8))]

families.why: Every call receives a distinct, valid public IPv4 address. The cache never hits, so each call pays the extra dictionary lookup, hashing, and LRU bookkeeping on top of the original overlap test.
families.size_meaning: Number of distinct IPs (n) – the generator returns up to 8 different IPs; the harness can repeat the list to reach n total calls.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    base = 20_000_001          # 20.0.0.1 as integer
    ips = []
    for i in range(min(n, 8)):
        # construct a.b.c.d from integer
        val = base + i
        a = (val >> 24) & 0xFF
        b = (val >> 16) & 0xFF
        c = (val >> 8) & 0xFF
        d = val & 0xFF
        ips.append([f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"])
    return ips

families.family: Many distinct, non‑excluded IPv4 addresses – each call misses the cache and pays the cache‑lookup overhead plus the full ipaddress/overlap work.
families.why: The cache can hold at most 1024 entries, but with a stream of unique addresses every call is a miss. The wrapper adds a dict lookup and function‑call overhead that the original code did not have.

def make(n):
    base = 1_000_000                # 1.0.0.0/8 is excluded, start above it
    ips = []
    for i in itertools.islice(range(base, base + max(1, min(n, 8))), max(1, min(n, 8))):
        a = (i >> 24) & 0xFF
        b = (i >> 16) & 0xFF
        c = (i >> 8) & 0xFF
        d = i & 0xFF
        ips.append([f'{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}'])
    return ips

families.why: Each distinct, non‑excluded address causes a cache miss. The LRU wrapper adds a dictionary lookup, key creation and possible eviction logic on top of the original linear scan over EXCLUDE_NETWORKS. With no repeats the base version avoids that overhead.

def make(n):
    calls = min(n, 8)
    # Use a public / non‑excluded block (8.0.0.0/8 is not in EXCLUDE_RANGES)
    return [[f"8.0.0.{i}"] for i in range(calls)]
